title: The Source and the Partial
english: To 'give drink to a child' who is thirsting; from that very 'source' she herself drank without 'water'. Thus you also find written concerning the Samaritan woman that she also 'left the water', in which it is written to draw water, 'and she went' to her own citizens to say to them, 'Come, see a man, who said to me all my sins' (John 4:28-29).

Rebecca therefore 'gives drink to the child' of Abraham, and not him alone, but also all those with him. 'And to the camels also' she... while drinking—for she 'went down to the spring'—but even if she carries 'water'... she was carrying, but 'to all' (Genesis 24:18-20).

'That which is known in part' and 'that which is prophesied in part' from the 'source' is 'water' having been filled. When therefore 'that which is in part' is abolished, 'the water is crushed.' And it is not destroyed, but [it goes] into the 'source'.

And I remind [you] of another doctrine spoken through other voices and material signs: we say that 'that which is in part' does not vanish, but is to be 'in part'; for an addition of the lacking honor has become.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
